description: One lifecycle action in flight, checked against every surface that renders it. `action` is the `pendingAction` the project service publishes; `family` is what both surfaces must say about it. Three families and they are not interchangeable: `progress` means the system is doing something and nothing is asked of the person, `attention` means a person must act, `failure` means it stopped. The TUI spelled progress as `Tone::Attention` (bold yellow) and the app as the `needs` token (amber) -- both the same colour they use for `attention` -- so a row the dashboard was busy with was painted exactly like a row waiting on a reply. The Rust half reads this file in native/crates/aimux/tests/transient_state_surfaces.rs and the app half in app/lib/transient-state.cross-surface.test.ts, so a surface that changes what it shows on its own fails here rather than drifting quietly. Scoped to the family rather than the exact colour, because the two surfaces render into a terminal and a browser and their palettes are not the same values; what has to agree is which of the three a state belongs to.
